page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 15 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.5 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor architecture (x86_64) running at 2.3 GHz, this server features 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver 2 dedicated virtual cores. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for specialized vector and matrix operations.

Performance benchmarks reveal a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench testing and strong single-threaded compression and decompression speeds, particularly with gzip and bzip3. However, due to its low core count, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the lower percentiles. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with large-block uncached read and write speeds registering in the bottom decile.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without the overhead of high vCPU counts. It features no bundled local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning external storage and networking must be provisioned separately. This configuration is best suited for memory-bound, single-threaded applications, lightweight database operations, basic caching, and small-scale text or prompt processing tasks that leverage its advanced CPU instruction sets.
